title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
hints: for a given bar, the biggest rectangle that uses its height as the limiting height extends left and right until it hits a shorter bar on either side - so you need, for every bar, the nearest shorter bar to its left and to its right
walk left to right keeping a stack of indices with increasing heights. what should happen when you encounter a bar shorter than the one on top of the stack?

when the current bar is shorter than the stack top, pop that top index - you now know its rectangle's right boundary (the current index) and, since the stack is increasing, its left boundary is whatever is now exposed on top of the stack (or the very start, if the stack is empty). compute its area as height * (currentIndex - newTopIndex - 1) and track the maximum

keep popping under that same rule, then push the current index; once you've scanned the whole array, push one final sentinel (a height of 0, or just treat the end as closing everything) to flush out and resolve every bar still left on the stack
commonMistakes: forgetting to flush the remaining stack after the scan ends, missing rectangles that extend to the very last bar
computing width using the wrong boundary indices (should be currentIndex - newTopOfStack - 1 after popping, not currentIndex - poppedIndex)
using a stack that isn't strictly increasing (not handling equal heights consistently), which can cause the same rectangle to be double counted or missed

content.problemStatement:
You're given an array of integers representing the heights of bars in a
histogram, each bar one unit wide and placed side by side.

**Return the area of the largest rectangle that can be formed using
only contiguous bars, where the rectangle's height is limited by the
shortest bar it spans.**
notes: all bars the same height (the widest rectangle spans everything)
a strictly increasing or strictly decreasing sequence of heights

sampleTestCases.explanation: bars at indices 2 and 3 (heights 5 and 6) form a rectangle of height 5 and width 2, area 10
either a single bar of height 4 and width 1 (area 4), or both bars at height 2 and width 2 (also area 4)
all four bars together form a rectangle of height 1 and width 4

optimal.pattern: monotonic increasing stack of indices, computing each bar's maximal rectangle the moment a shorter bar forces it to 'close'

bruteForce.approach: for every pair of left and right boundaries, find the minimum height in between and compute the resulting area, keeping the maximum
bruteForce.time: O(n^2), or O(n^3) if the minimum is recomputed by scanning each time
